strengths: The method addresses a practically important problem and demonstrates dataset distillation at ImageNet-1K scale using pretrained features, representative feature targets, and class-specific BatchNorm regularization.

Table I shows consistent improvements over the strengthened SRe2L baseline. On ImageNet-1K, accuracy improves from 54.4% to 57.6% at 50 images per class and from 58.3% to 60.7% at 100. Reporting both published and replicated baseline results, with explanations of training changes, improves transparency.

Experiments cover three ImageNet-derived datasets, multiple compression budgets, repeated evaluations, and transfer to larger ResNets. Component ablations, regularization sweeps, and qualitative examples provide useful supporting evidence. The paper appropriately credits SRe2L, the barycenter algorithms, and the POT library.
weaknesses: The central novelty is insufficiently established. Equation 4 approximates one empirical distribution per class with a limited number of atoms. With squared-Euclidean Wasserstein distance and freely optimized atom masses, the stated unregularized objective reduces to k-means quantization. The paper neither explains this relationship nor compares against k-means feature targets using the same image-recovery pipeline. Consequently, the advantage specifically attributable to Wasserstein barycenters remains unclear.

Table III supports the class-specific BatchNorm modification more strongly than the Wasserstein component. At 10 images per class, cross-entropy plus class-specific BatchNorm already achieves 64.0/41.3/37.4% on ImageNette/Tiny ImageNet/ImageNet-1K, versus 64.8/41.8/38.2% for the complete method. Holding cross-entropy and BatchNorm fixed, adding barycenter matching yields 63.9/42.1/37.9%. These modest, mixed increments warrant stronger isolation of the proposed metric, including a comparable MMD objective and ablations at larger budgets.

Important implementation details remain unresolved. Section III-B describes entropically regularized transport, whereas the supplementary algorithms specify unregularized transport problems; the entropy coefficient, initialization, and stopping criteria are not supplied. Moreover, the learned atom masses disappear from Algorithm 1's output, and their use in student sampling or training is unspecified. This leaves the connection between the optimized probability measure and the actual synthetic training distribution incomplete.

The comparative efficiency claim lacks adequate measurements. Table IV reports only an image-update timing and memory figure for 64×64 ImageNette, without competing methods. The supplementary 14-hour ImageNet experiment establishes feasibility but does not clarify the costs of teacher training, feature extraction, barycenter computation, and relabeling or demonstrate an efficiency advantage over SRe2L.
